source.title: CoE: Chain-of-Explanation via Automatic Visual Concept Circuit Description and Polysemanticity Quantification
source.authors: Wen-Long Yu; Qi-Long Wang; Chuang Liu; Dong Li; Qing-Hua Hu

page_placements.theme: What units encode, and how polysemantic or describable they are, varies with depth (vision and audio classifiers; LM neuron roles in the original SoLU source)

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses automatically generated descriptions of image patches and CPE scores to examine visual-concept polysemanticity, rather than the original neuron-visualization method.
record.gate_note: Qualifying results concern visual concept channels, their generated concept atoms and CPE measurements. The local-explanation score comparisons are not rows because they measure explanation quality, not polysemanticity itself. The cited estimate of an average of 13 concept atoms per ResNet152 channel is not counted as a study result.
record.test_reason: The study measures how many distinct concepts ResNet152, ResNet50/101 and CLIP-ResNet50 channels encode. It uses LVLM descriptions of CRP-selected patches and an entropy score (CPE), a different method from feature visualization aimed at the same question. It also shows that this measure shifts with the XAI method and the CPE formula.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that visual concepts are polysemantic and that CPE quantifies this, with CPE validated by 75% human agreement. They report CPE peaking in intermediate layers and rising with model depth. Their main claim is that CPDF disentanglement and filtering improves LLM-generated local explanations, by an average absolute 36% in explainability scores.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CRP-selected image patches, LVLM-generated concept atoms, semantic clustering and CPE; it does not reproduce the original source methods.
record.method_sensitivity: CPE trends differ across relevance-based, activation-based and maximum-mutual-information-based XAI methods. CPE also changes with semantic clustering and padding refinement. Reported CPE varies by stage, model depth and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet152 (and CLIP-ResNet50), averaged CPE peaks at stage 3 and is lower in the first and last stages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In CNN image classifiers, polysemanticity is highest in intermediate layers.

record.problems: Polysemanticity is inferred from LVLM-generated descriptions of 15 selected image patches per concept, rather than validated by causal tests of each concept's function. The text does not report uncertainty estimates for CPE. CPE results vary with the XAI method, and some comparisons are reported only in figures.

untested.parts: The InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 and the cat-face/car-front example; causal tests that a channel responds to each unrelated input.
Activation function (e.g. SoLU), regularization, interventions that lower polysemanticity, and any performance cost.
Which part of the activation range is examined (only the top-15 patches are used throughout).

missing.what: Layer-wise averaged CPE for ResNet152, peaking at stage 3 and lower at stages 1 and 4.
Concept 141 (lobster): all 15 patches identical, CPE 0.70 after padding but 1 under the clustered formula. This is a monosemantic example and a measurement artefact.
missing.locator: Table S8 row 1; Sec. S3.1, S4.1

missing.what: 75% agreement between CPE and human pairwise polysemanticity judgments on 300 VC pairs.
Per-stage CLIP vs ResNet50 CPE, with the same intermediate-peak pattern.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mislabelled Table S8 concepts. The atom list for 366 actually belongs to 121, and 366 is a coherent muzzle channel. CPE is normalized entropy over LVLM-generated attribute words, so its floor is high and it counts attributes such as colour and material. It is a weak proxy for unrelated-input selectivity. There are no uncertainty estimates, and the depth differences are tiny.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the specific InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 or verify neural responses to the example cat-face and car-front inputs.
Language models and transformer MLP neurons.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons, or by superposition.
Polysemanticity caused by initialization, regularization or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Does not test activation-function or regularization changes, SoLU, whether polysemanticity can be reduced by an intervention, or the associated performance cost.
Does not establish whether canonical mixed-response neurons detect one underlying feature or whether genuinely unrelated mixtures are rare.
Does not vary activation-range cutoffs or compare alternative explanation-scoring criteria; it compares XAI methods and CPE formulations.

rows.check: Wrong content. Table S8 lists concepts 141, 366, 1681, 121 with CPE rising 0.70, 0.77, 0.85, 0.89. So concept 366 (CPE 0.77) is the dog-muzzle channel: dog, muzzle, black/brown, plastic/metal/leather. The dogs/peppers/deer/truck atoms belong to concept 121 (r3). Concept 366 is one coherent concept with material variants, not an unrelated mixture.
